step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify the overall system context: Cookpad's security log monitoring architecture divided into Collection, Retention, and Analysis phases.
2. Collection phase nodes: EC2 (0), Firehose (1), CloudTrail (2), ThirdParty service (3), and Lambda Collection (4).
3. Retention phase node: Central S3 bucket (5) storing ~330M logs / 270GB monthly.
4. Analysis phase nodes: Lambda Top (6) for real-time alerting, Lambda Middle (7) for feeding search engine, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch (8) for log indexing, and Athena (9) for ad-hoc queries.
5. Map edges directly from the visual diagram and audio transcript to model data and control flows.

graph.name: Cookpad Log Collection, Retention, and Analysis Architecture
graph.notes: Serverless security log monitoring architecture handling 330 million logs (270 GB) per month at extremely low cost (~$2/month).

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Sends syslog messages from instances to Kinesis Data Firehose.

nodes.name: Firehose
nodes.notes: Streams syslog messages directly into Amazon S3.

nodes.name: CloudTrail
nodes.notes: Delivers AWS API and management audit logs directly into Amazon S3.

nodes.name: 3rd Party Service
nodes.notes: External third-party services generating log events.

nodes.name: Lambda Collection
nodes.notes: Transforms third-party log data before storing it in S3.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central log retention store with S3 Lifecycle policies for cost optimization (~330M logs / 270 GB).

nodes.name: Lambda Analysis Top
nodes.notes: Performs near real-time analysis and sends alerts (e.g., Slack notifications).

nodes.name: Lambda Analysis Middle
nodes.notes: Processes S3 logs for ingestion into search and visualization tools.

nodes.name: Elasticsearch
nodes.notes: Indexes log data for search capabilities via Graylog / Elasticsearch.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Performs direct ad-hoc SQL queries on long-term log data stored in S3.

edges.notes: Firehose writes log stream to S3.
CloudTrail delivers audit logs directly to S3.
Third-party service triggers Lambda function for log ingestion.
Lambda Collection writes transformed third-party logs to S3.
New log object in S3 triggers Lambda for real-time alert processing.
New log object in S3 triggers Lambda for indexing.
Lambda forwards log data to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.
Athena queries raw log data stored in S3.
